people.summary: Father of Gertrud Elise Becker (Christa's mother), so Thomas Kohlmann's maternal great-grandfather.
people.story: Father of Gertrud Elise Becker (Christa's mother), so Thomas Kohlmann's maternal great-grandfather. Kaufmann (merchant). Born 5 January 1875 in Herzberg, Kreis Schweinitz (Herzberg on the Black Elster), and died at home, Rothermundtstraße 5, Dresden, on 9 January 1938, aged 63, according to his civil death entry (Dresden V 1938 Nr. 52).[^anc-death-1938] The 2007 family chart has the two days the other way round (born 9 January, died 5 January); the record is preferred. The chart gives pneumonia as the cause.[^ahnentafel-2007] In 1905 he lived at Ziegelstraße 2 in Dresden, where Gertrud was born and where he reported her birth himself.[^anc-birth-1905] By 1926 the family lived at Rothermundtstraße 5 in Striesen, where he kept an ironmonger's shop on the ground floor ("Becker, R., Eisenwhdlg.").[^slub-dresden-1938] He was a witness at Gertrud's wedding to Alwin Eifler on 2 October 1926, aged 51.[^anc-marriage-1926] He was cremated at the Dresden crematorium in January 1938, certificate 60603.[^anc-cremation-1938] The chart records two sisters; a handwritten note names one as Marie (married surname perhaps Wettlitz) of Rothermundtstraße 5.

Her civil death entry calls her Clara Elise Becker née Just, Hausfrau, born 1 December 1880 in Raun, Kreis Oelsnitz im Vogtland (birth registered at Bad Elster, Nr. 132).[^findbuch-death-1954] She married the merchant Richard Hermann Becker and lived in Dresden. Widowed in 1938, she later lived with her daughter's family at Wilthener Straße 19 in Bautzen, where she died at 2:10 in the morning of 27 December 1954, aged 74. Gertrud reported the death.[^findbuch-death-1954] The family chart says she was one of eight Just children (two sisters and five brothers) and died of heart failure.[^ahnentafel-2007]

people.story: Father of Christa Kohlmann and Sigrid Michaelis, and Thomas Kohlmann's maternal grandfather. Born 7 October 1892 in Sohland an der Spree; his marriage entry gives the place and cites his Sohland birth entry.[^anc-marriage-1926] A Weickert & Eifler saddlery and upholstery shop already existed in Bautzen in 1921, run by the master saddler Bruno Weickert at Löbauer Straße 10.[^anc-bautzen-1921] On 2 October 1926 Alwin, a "Fabrikant" living at Wendischer Graben 3 in Bautzen, married Gertrud Elise Becker at the Dresden V registry office (1926 Nr. 352). The witnesses were Ernst Eifler, a farmer of Sohland an der Spree Nr. 247, aged 61 (probably his father), and the bride's father.[^anc-marriage-1926] From 1928 he is listed as sole owner (Inhaber) of the Stahldrahtmatratzenfabrik Weickert & Eifler, with the factory at Gnaschwitz and his home and office at Neusalzaer Straße 38.[^slub-bautzen-1928] By 1935 the firm was at Martin-Mutschmann-Straße 19 (today Wilthener Straße 19), a house he owned by 1938.[^anc-bautzen-1935][^slub-bautzen-1938] The family chart says he died on 18 December 1968 of a basal skull fracture after a car accident, aged 76, and names his siblings as Max, Alfred and Martha.[^ahnentafel-2007] His death is not in the Bautzen city register for 1968, so it was probably registered where the accident happened; Gertrud is recorded as widowed in 1973.[^findbuch-index-1968][^findbuch-death-1973] See the Weickert & Eifler page for the full story of the firm.

people.summary: Mother of Christa Kohlmann and Sigrid Michaelis.
people.story: Mother of Christa Kohlmann and Sigrid Michaelis, and Thomas Kohlmann's maternal grandmother. Born 22 January 1905 at Ziegelstraße 2 in Dresden, daughter of the merchant Richard Hermann Becker, who reported the birth (Dresden I 1905 Nr. 165).[^anc-birth-1905] Living with her parents at Rothermundtstraße 5 in Dresden-Striesen, she married Alwin Eifler on 2 October 1926 at the Dresden V registry office, aged 21.[^anc-marriage-1926] A Weickert & Eifler invoice of 9 April 1943 carries her signed receipt: "Betrag dankend erhalten. Gertrud Eifler. d. 28.4.1943." That shows she signed for the firm; whether she kept its books is not recorded.[^weickert-invoice-1943] In 1954 she reported her mother's death at the family house, Wilthener Straße 19, Bautzen.[^findbuch-death-1954] She died there, a widow, at 3:00 in the morning of 11 December 1973, aged 68 (Bautzen 1973 Nr. 1052).[^findbuch-death-1973] The family chart gives cancer as the cause.[^ahnentafel-2007]

people.summary: Thomas's father, Herbert Kohlmann, known in the family in English as Herbert Coleman. He married Christa Eifler in Bautzen on 24 July 1952.
people.story: Thomas's father, Herbert Kohlmann. The family gives his name in English as Herbert Coleman.[^family-correction-2026-11-26] He married Elise Christa Eifler, daughter of Alwin and Gertrud Eifler of the Bautzen mattress firm Weickert & Eifler, on 24 July 1952 in Bautzen; the date is on the 2007 family chart.[^ahnentafel-2007] They had three children, Thomas, Matthias and Sabine. Deceased. Earlier versions of this site gave his first name wrongly, a mix-up with Christa's father, Alwin Eifler, and the family corrected it on 26 November 2026. Herbert's birth, death, occupation and parents are not yet known. The Bautzen marriage entry of 1952 would name his parents, his birthplace and his occupation. Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a Bautzen butcher born in 1883, is a possible candidate for his father because of the surname, the town and his age, but nothing links them.

people.story: On 2 October 1926 a farmer named Ernst Eifler, of Sohland an der Spree Nr. 247, aged 61, signed as a witness at the Dresden wedding of Alwin Eifler and Gertrud Becker.[^anc-marriage-1926] Alwin was born in Sohland in 1892, so Ernst is probably his father, but no record seen so far says so. Alwin's Sohland birth entry or baptism would settle it. The 2007 family chart names Alwin's brothers Max and Alfred and his sister Martha.[^ahnentafel-2007] If Ernst was Alwin's father he was theirs too, and they are drawn that way here; the dashed lines show that this is not yet proven.

people.disambiguator: a lead for Herbert Kohlmann's family
people.summary: Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a butcher, was born on 21 September 1883 at Kötzschau near Lawalde (Kreis Löbau) and died in Bautzen on 27 February 1972, still living at Schäfferstraße 6, his address since 1925. He married Marie Ida Jurack in 1914. Same surname and town as Herbert Kohlmann, Thomas's father, and of an age to be his father, but nothing links him to the family. He is shown as a suspected relative only.
people.story: In 1921 the Bautzen address book lists "Kohlmann, Alwin, Fleischergeselle" (journeyman butcher) at Holzmarkt 27, in the rear building, first floor.[^anc-bautzen-1921-kohlmann] In 1924 he is a butcher (Fleischer) at Holzmarkt 27, ground floor.[^anc-bautzen-1924-kohlmann] From 1925 he lives at Schäfferstraße 6, and he is there in every book seen up to 1938.[^anc-bautzen-1925-kohlmann][^slub-bautzen-1928][^anc-bautzen-1935-kohlmann][^slub-bautzen-1938] He is the only Alwin Kohlmann in each book, and there is no second, younger Kohlmann butcher. Thomas Kohlmann's father was Herbert Kohlmann, who married Christa Eifler in Bautzen in 1952. This Alwin, born in 1883, could belong to Herbert's parents' generation, but nothing found so far links him to Herbert or to the family. (An older idea that Thomas's father was called Alvin, and might be this Alwin, came from a mix-up with Christa's father Alwin Eifler and is closed.) The Bautzen death name index for 1972 lists "Kohlmann, Ernst Alwin", who died on 27 February 1972, death register number 185.[^findbuch-death-index-1972-kohlmann] He is the only Alwin Kohlmann in the Bautzen death indexes from 1946 to 1979, so he is probably the butcher, but the index gives no age or address. The register entry itself would give his birth and next of kin.[^findbuch-death-indexes-1946-1972] His death entry in the Bautzen register for 1972 settles who he was: Ernst Alwin Kohlmann of Schäfferstraße 6, the same house as in the address books, died on 27 February 1972. He was born on 21 September 1883 at Kötzschau, a hamlet near Lawalde in Kreis Löbau, and was married to Marie Ida Kohlmann née Jurack; the marriage was registered at Malschwitz in 1914.[^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] Marie Ida died in Bautzen less than a year later, on 20 January 1973.[^findbuch-death-indexes-1946-1972] The entry does not name his parents or any children. A second Kohlmann from the same village died in Bautzen in 1980: Ernestine Hedwig Kissal née Kohlmann, born on 15 September 1897 at Kleindehsa, the village that Kötzschau belongs to. She married Ernst Hermann Kissal at Lawalde in 1926 and lived at Mättigstraße 17.[^findbuch-death-register-1980-40] She was probably Alwin's younger sister, which would make this Bautzen Kohlmann family one from the Lawalde parish near Löbau.

openQuestions.question: Was he Herbert Kohlmann's father? The 1952 marriage entry (Standesamt Bautzen) names Herbert's parents and would show whether this family is connected.
Who were his parents? His 1914 marriage entry (Malschwitz Nr. 9/1914) and his 1883 birth entry (Lawalde Nr. 71/1883) name them.
Was Ernestine Hedwig Kissal née Kohlmann (1897 to 1980) his sister? Her 1926 Lawalde marriage entry (Nr. 4/1926) names her parents.

people.disambiguator: tax official in Döbeln, a lead for Brigitte's family
people.summary: Max Woltmann, a tax official, was the only Woltmann in the Döbeln address books of 1925 and 1939, at the same house both times. Rita was born a Woltmann in Döbeln in 1956, so he may be Brigitte's father or another close relative. Not proven.
people.story: The Döbeln address book for 1925 lists "Woltmann Max, Steuerassist." (tax assistant) at Kleinbauchlitzer Straße 20. He is the only Woltmann in the book.[^slub-doebeln-1925] In 1939 the book lists "Woltmann, Max, Steuersekretär" (tax secretary) at Grimmaische Straße 20, again the only Woltmann.[^slub-doebeln-1939] The 1939 book heads Grimmaische Straße "vorher Kleinbauchlitzer Straße" (formerly Kleinbauchlitzer Straße), so this is the same house: he lived at No. 20 from at least 1925 to 1939 and was promoted from assistant to secretary.[^slub-doebeln-1939] There was no Woltmann in Döbeln in 1900-01, so he came to the town after 1900.[^slub-doebeln-1900] Rita was born in Döbeln in 1956 with her mother Brigitte's surname, Woltmann.[^family-testimony] With so rare a name, Max is probably Brigitte's father or grandfather, but no record seen so far links them. Brigitte's birth entry would settle it. Ancestry's copies of the same two books show the same entries; Ancestry has no birth, marriage or death record for him, and none for Brigitte.[^anc-doebeln-1925][^anc-doebeln-1939]

people.story: Max Bruno Weickert, master saddler, was the Weickert of Weickert & Eifler. Born on 2 December 1892 in Großschönau near Zittau, he ran the saddlery and upholstery shop at Löbauer Straße 10 that carried the firm's name in 1921. By 1928 Alwin Eifler was the sole owner. Bruno died at home, Fischergasse 31 in Bautzen, on 26 March 1956.[^findbuch-death-register-1956-225][^anc-bautzen-1921]

On this tree he is drawn as a child of Ernst Eifler, the Sohland farmer who was probably Alwin's father; that link is not proven, so the line is dashed. A Max Eifler lived in Bautzen at Paulistraße 32 and is listed right under Alwin in the 1928 address book, but his 1978 death entry shows he was Max Oswald Eifler, born on 2 March 1892 at Oberrennersdorf, seven months before Alwin and in another village, so he cannot be Alwin's full brother.[^findbuch-death-register-1978-704]

openQuestions.question: When and where was Martha born? Alwin's Sohland birth entry (1892) and the Sohland church books would give the parents and the other children.

people.summary: Richard Becker's sister, named in a handwritten note on the 2007 family chart, with the address Rothermundtstraße 5 in Dresden. Her married surname is perhaps Wettlitz.
people.story: The 2007 family chart records two sisters of Richard Becker, and a handwritten note names one of them as Marie, with a married surname that seems to read Wettlitz (or Wettlich, or Wettnitz), at Rothermundtstraße 5 in Dresden, Richard's own address.[^ahnentafel-2007] She was probably born in Herzberg on the Black Elster, like Richard, between about 1870 and 1885, but no record of her has been found yet. The Dresden house registers for Rothermundtstraße 5 in 1938 and 1943 list nobody under a W name, so she may have lived there earlier or later.[^slub-dresden-1938] She is drawn beside Richard with a dashed line because no record yet proves the link.

openQuestions.question: What was her married name? The Dresden address books from 1925 to 1943 and the Herzberg church books are the next places to look.

people.summary: The 2007 family chart records that Richard Becker had two sisters. This is the second one; her name is not on the page the family holds.
people.story: The 2007 family chart records two sisters of Richard Becker. One is Marie; the other is not named on page 1, the only page the family has.[^ahnentafel-2007] Page 2 of the chart may name her.

openQuestions.question: What was her name? Page 2 of the 2007 chart, or the Herzberg church books, would tell.

people.disambiguator: wife of Alwin Kohlmann the butcher
people.summary: Wife of Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a Bautzen butcher who is one of the leads for Herbert Kohlmann's family. Born at Briesing in 1887, married at Malschwitz in 1914, died in Bautzen in 1973. Not proven to be family.
people.story: Marie Ida Jurack was born on 5 February 1887 at Briesing near Malschwitz, north of Bautzen, and married Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a butcher, at Malschwitz in 1914 (register Nr. 9/1914). She was his widow when he died in February 1972 and died herself on 20 January 1973 in Bautzen, living at Am Stadtwall 1.[^findbuch-death-register-1973-55][^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] Briesing was a Sorbian village: when Arnošt Muka counted the villages in 1884 and 1885, 176 of its 183 people were Sorbs, and Jurack is a Sorbian surname (from Jurij, George).[^wikipedia-briesing] Whether her own family spoke Sorbian at home is not yet known. Her husband is one of the leads being checked for Herbert Kohlmann's family. Nothing links either of them to the family, so she is shown as a suspected relative only, not as an ancestor.

openQuestions.question: Did she and Alwin have children? The Malschwitz marriage entry (1914) gives both sets of parents, and Bautzen births from 1914 would show any children.

facts.label: Marriage
facts.value: Married Ernst Hermann Kissal, registered at Lawalde, Kreis Löbau, Nr. 4/1926. He was still living when she died in 1980.

people.summary: Born at Kleindehsa in 1897, the village Kötzschau belongs to, where Alwin Kohlmann the butcher was born in 1883. Probably his sister; not proven.
people.story: Ernestine Hedwig Kohlmann was born on 15 September 1897 at Kleindehsa, Kreis Löbau. She married Ernst Hermann Kissal at Lawalde in 1926 (Nr. 4/1926) and died in Bautzen on 14 January 1980, living at Mättigstraße 17; her husband was still alive.[^findbuch-death-register-1980-40] Alwin Kohlmann the butcher was born in 1883 at Kötzschau, a hamlet of Kleindehsa, and registered at the same office, Lawalde.[^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] Same surname, same village, fourteen years apart: she was probably his sister, but no record seen yet names their parents.

openQuestions.question: Who were her parents? The Lawalde marriage entry of 1926 (Nr. 4) would name them, and so would answer whether she was Alwin's sister.

people.summary: Richter (village judge) of Kötzschau, father of Gottfried Kohlmann, who bought the Kleindehsa inn in 1787.
people.story: In 1787 Gottfried Kohlmann, "son of the judge Johann Kohlmann of Kötschau", bought the Kretscham at Kleindehsa.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] The village judge (Richter) presided over the village court and spoke for the village to the manor. The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

people.summary: Son of the village judge Johann Kohlmann of Kötzschau. In 1787 he bought the Kretscham, the village inn of Kleindehsa, for 600 Taler; the family kept it for about 150 years.
people.story: In 1787 Gottfried Kohlmann, son of the judge Johann Kohlmann of Kötzschau, bought the Kretschamgut, the village inn with its farm, from the widow of an appeal court councillor, von Heldreich, for 600 Taler. From then on the inn stayed in the Kohlmann family for 150 years.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] Forty years earlier, in 1748 and 1749, the manor had built the inn new and sold it to an innkeeper who had to hand over the tongue of every ox he slaughtered and pour only Löbau beer. The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

people.story: The village chronicle says Karl August Reinhold Kohlmann took over the inn in 1885.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] Alwin Kohlmann the butcher was born two years earlier, in 1883, at Kötzschau, a hamlet of the same village.[^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

openQuestions.question: Was he the father of Alwin Kohlmann (born 1883 at Kötzschau) and of Ernestine Hedwig (born 1897 at Kleindehsa)? Alwin's Lawalde birth entry, 1883 Nr. 71, names his parents.

people.disambiguator: owner of the Kleindehsa inn after 1927
people.summary: Became owner of the Kretscham some years after 1927; after his death his brother Ernst and a daughter kept it until 1959.
people.story: In 1927 a hall was opened on the south side of the Kretscham. Some years later Gustav Kohlmann became the owner, and after his death his brother Ernst and his daughter held it until 1959.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] From 1958 the Senftenberg brown coal combine ran a holiday camp in a side wing, and after 1959 the whole inn passed to the combine. The Kretscham burned down on the evening of 29 January 1997 and was pulled down. The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

openQuestions.question: Gustav's brother Ernst: could he be Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, the Bautzen butcher? Nothing links them yet.
